channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD slips below $60.50 amid rising inflation concerns
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) loses ground after registering gains the previous day, trading around $60.30 per troy ounce during Asian hours on Friday. Silver price retreats as rising crude oil costs, driven by fears of a deteriorating conflict between the US and Iran, reignite broader inflation concerns.

item.title: United States Dollar Index sits near March 2025 highs, above 102.00 ahead of US NFP
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which tracks the Greenback against a basket of currencies, attracts buyers for the fifth straight day and climbs back above the 102.00 mark during the Asian session on Friday.

item.title: Canadian Dollar falls as oil prices dip, US Dollar gains strength
item.description: USD/CAD rebounds after registering losses in the previous day, trading around 1.4230 during the Asian hours on Friday. The currency pair continues to gain ground as the US Dollar (USD) receives strong support.

item.title: WTI holds steady near $92.00 as US weighs sending more troops to Middle East
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI), the US crude oil benchmark, is trading around $91.75 during the early Asian trading hours on Friday. WTI flatlines after a two-day gain as the United States (US) mulled sending another aircraft carrier group to the Middle East.

item.title: British Pound struggles near June 26 lows as USD retains bullish tone ahead of US NFP
item.description: The GBP/USD pair languished near its lowest level since June 26, touched the previous day's low, trading below the 1.3200 mark during the Asian session on Friday amid a bullish US Dollar (USD).

item.title: US may send third aircraft carrier and 10,000 troops to Middle East
item.description: US official said that the Pentagon may soon send a third aircraft-carrier strike group and 10,000 sailors and Marines to the Persian Gulf, the Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday.

item.title: US pressures EU to tap emergency diesel stockpiles
item.description: The US President Donald Trump administration told European allies to release diesel from national emergency stockpiles, Bloomberg reported on Thursday.

item.title: The Japanese Yen gains little from a hot Tokyo inflation report
item.description: Tokyo's core inflation rate came in at 2.7% against a 2.4% forecast, a beat that should have done more for the Yen than it did. USD/JPY slipped back below 158.00 on the release and is still up on the week.

item.title: Gold recovers above $4,150 as US yields retreat ahead of US September jobs data
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) rises to near $4,180 during the early Asian session on Friday. The precious metal rebounds as US Treasury bond yields retreat from multi-decade highs.

item.title: Fed’s Logan: Policy rate must increase by additional 50 bps or more
item.description: Federal Reserve (Fed) Bank of Dallas President Lorie Logan said on Thursday that the central bank will need to raise short-term borrowing costs by at least another half of a percentage point to turn monetary policy "modestly restrictive" and get inflation back on track to the target.

item.title: Breaking: Japan’s Tokyo CPI inflation climbs 2.7% in September
item.description: The headline Tokyo Consumer Price Index (CPI) for September rose 2.7% YoY as compared to 1.9% in the previous month, the Statistics Bureau of Japan showed on Friday.

item.title: Australian Dollar drifts toward 0.69 as USD shrugs off Fed patience
item.description: The Aussie Dollar drifts lower, down 0.26% against the US Dollar, as the latter extends its gains for the fourth straight day amid continued trimming of Fed-hawkish bets, while Fed policymakers suggest patience is warranted ahead of the October 28 meeting. The AUD/USD trades at 0.6928.

item.title: The Japanese Yen weakens as traders pare Bank of Japan October hike bets
item.description: The Yen is falling on the timetable of the Bank of Japan (BoJ) rather than on Japanese inflation. The BoJ published its September meeting summary at 23:50 GMT on Wednesday, and traders cut bets on an October follow-up.

item.title: The New Zealand Dollar extends its slide as the US Dollar hits a yearly high
item.description: Five losing weeks in a row and most of a sixth have taken NZD/USD to its lowest since the Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) last cut rates, in November 2025. The RBNZ has raised its rate twice since, to 2.75%, and traders have built up bets on a third hike on October 28.

item.title: The Euro sells off hard as the French-German bond gap widens
item.description: France unveiled a 2027 budget on Thursday aimed at reassuring the investors who lend it money, and EUR/USD is heading for its biggest one-day loss since June 17. Those investors already charge France 130 basis points more than Germany to borrow for ten years, the widest gap since 2012.

item.title: The British Pound slides again as UK government bonds sell off
item.description: Britain's 30-year gilt yield went above 6% on Thursday for the first time since 1998, and GBP/USD fell to its lowest since late June. Bank of England (BoE) external member Mann said in a speech the same day that UK financial conditions aren't tight enough.

item.title: Gold defies US Dollar surge as US yield slide revives Bullion demand
item.description: Gold price drifted higher, posting modest gains of over 0.40% on Thursday as US Treasury yields dove after Wednesday's inflation data, triggering a trimming of hawkish Fed bets for the October meeting. The XAU/USD trades at $4,175, up 0.4%.

item.title: Fed’s Jefferson says US economy is near maximum employment
item.description: Federal Reserve (Fed) Vice Chairman Philip Jefferson said Thursday that “inflation has resulted from a cascade of shocks” at the Darden School of Business at the University of Virginia in Charlottesville, Virginia.

item.title: Dollar Index breaks its June peak as the Euro sinks on dearer Crude Oil
item.description: The odds of an October Fed rate hike have roughly halved since Monday, and the Dollar Index has risen on every one of those days. It trades near 102.10, its highest since April 2025. The index is moving with Crude Oil and the Euro rather than with the odds for the Fed's next meeting.

item.title: Crude Oil extends its rally as the Pentagon adds another carrier group
item.description: A report that the Pentagon is sending a third aircraft carrier strike group to the Middle East has added a second leg to Thursday's rally in Crude Oil.

item.title: US Dollar Index Price Forecast: DXY reaches fresh yearly high, but RSI turns overbought
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) rally gathers pace on Thursday, climbing to a fresh year-to-date high as resilient US economic growth, a firm labour market and stubborn inflation support expectations of further monetary policy tightening by the Federal Reserve (Fed).

item.title: Fed’s Kashkari keeps October meeting open, still sees more hikes ahead
item.description: Minneapolis Federal Reserve (Fed) President Neel Kashkari said on Thursday he is unsure about an October rate hike but added that he is “open-minded about how fast the Fed should raise interest rates.”

item.title: Fed’s Jefferson signals patience as next rate move stays data-driven
item.description: Vice Chairman of the Federal Reserve (Fed) Philip Jefferson said on Thursday that the Fed "is fully committed to returning inflation to 2% target” and that future interest rate decisions “should be driven by data.”

item.title: Banxico survey sees lower inflation, stronger growth and 6.50% hold
item.description: A Bank of Mexico (Banxico) survey of private economists revised down headline and core inflation forecasts, updated projections for the USD/MXN exchange rate, and revised projections for future interest rates set by the Mexican institution.

item.title: Mexican Peso rout deepens as USD/MXN blasts 18.30
item.description: The Mexican Peso (MXN) collapses on Monday, extending its depreciation by over 1.50% as the Greenback strengthens sharply amid growing fears that the Middle East conflict will be prolonged, keeping energy prices under pressure.

item.title: Forex Today: US NFP takes centre stage
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) has advanced further on Thursday, trading in levels last seen in early April 2025 on the back of the marked improvement in the sentiment surrounding the US Dollar, geopolitical uncertainty and renewed concerns over the French economy.

item.title: Gold struggles as elevated US Treasury yields outweigh dovish Fed repricing
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) treads water on Thursday as a stronger US Dollar (USD) and elevated US Treasury yields limit the upside.

item.title: Japanese Yen recovers as intervention risk offsets US Dollar strength
item.description: USD/JPY reverses its earlier gains on Thursday as traders hesitate to push the pair higher amid the risk of intervention by Japanese authorities. This allows the Japanese Yen (JPY) to regain some ground even as the US Dollar (USD) climbs to a fresh year-to-date high.

item.title: Australian Dollar weakens as robust US data, rising US yields overshadow RBA rate hike
item.description: AUD/USD falls to around 0.6910 on Thursday at the time of writing, down 0.48% on the day. The Australian Dollar (AUD) loses ground against the US Dollar (USD) despite the Reserve Bank of Australia’s (RBA) decision to raise interest rates this week, as rising US Treasury yields support the Greenback.

item.title: British Pound buckles as DXY nears 102 on US jobs, factory strength
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) dives by over 0.44% on Thursday, as business activity in the manufacturing sector remains solid in the US, while US jobs data confirmed the strength of the labor market. Consequently, this pushed US yields and the US Dollar higher.
